source.title: Spatial Induction Heads: In-Context Learning of Multidimensional Cellular Automata
source.authors: Kimia Kazemian; Meng Xu; John Thickstun; Sarah Dean

record.tranche_reason: Tests a spatial gather-and-match analogue of induction with attention alignment and ablations, rather than the original sequential induction-head method.
record.gate_note: The study trains two-layer transformers on cellular automata and reports predictive performance and mechanistic measurements. The attention-alignment and ablation values in Figures 3 are figure-only; the text describes their direction but gives no exact values. Cited results and theoretical constructions are not empirical rows. The paper does not report training-time induction-head formation, training-loss bumps, or in-context-learning transitions.
record.test_reason: The study trains two-layer transformers on serialized 1D and 2D cellular automata, a new modality, and tests whether they learn an induction-style circuit. Layer 1 gathers a spatial neighbourhood, a generalization of the previous-token head, and Layer 2 matches against precedents and retrieves their successors. Its evidence is attention alignment plus targeted ablations with matched random controls (Fig. 3, App. I.5–I.6). It is a new-setting result on the mechanism (V1) and on universality across modalities (V4), not a reproduction of the original sequential method, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it leaves out the theory. The authors also prove two explicit constructions of the spatial gather, with positional width independent of grid size and horizon. They show the Layer-2 match implements Bayesian counting, so the circuit can approximate the Dirichlet posterior or predict deterministic rules exactly. Empirically they claim held-out-rule generalization, with attention, ablation and linear-probe evidence consistent with gather-and-match.
record.recipe_differences: Uses spatial cellular-automaton tasks with learned absolute positions, a first-layer spatial gather, and a second-layer precedent match. It is not the original sequential induction-head training or measurement setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The experiments vary cellular-automaton setting (1D binary, 1D ternary, 2D von Neumann) and layer-1 design (Shared-head or Dedicated-heads).

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer transformers infer unseen cellular-automaton rules in context. They reach near-perfect deterministic accuracy on held-out rules and come within 0.005 nats KL of the k-gram Bayes reference on stochastic rules.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small transformers trained on serialized multidimensional data learn near-Bayes-optimal in-context rule inference.

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: Attention alignment and ablation outcomes are shown in figures without exact values or uncertainty estimates. The reported experiments use cellular automata and two layer-1 designs, without a model-family or training-run sweep.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Figure 4 layerwise probe results and additional predictive metrics in Tables 13-14, including deterministic sequence accuracy and stochastic teacher-forced metrics. Figure 5 and Appendix Figures 6-8 are qualitative t-SNE visualizations. No training-time loss or head-formation results are reported.

untested.parts: The study does not use attention-only models: the Shared-head design needs an L1 MLP, and both designs have an L2 MLP. It does not test the ordinary token-sequence [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying, or composition with a literal previous-token head. The L1 head instead gathers previous-timestep spatial neighbours.
No training-time dynamics, no head-onset timing, and no loss bump.
No large models and no language-model in-context learning.
No variation across model families, sizes or multiple training runs; only two-layer models with two L1 designs are tested.
No manipulation of data or training properties against whether or when the circuit forms.
Few-shot task learning and copying are not contrasted.

record.verdict_notes: All mechanistic evidence (Fig. 3) is figure-only, with no values or uncertainty, and comes from a single training run per configuration. The circuit needs an L1 MLP in the Shared-head design, so it does not speak to the attention-only part of V1. The Figure 4 probe results are declared in rows_left_out; they would further support V1/V4 layerwise structure. Predictive rows have been moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or the ordinary sequential [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying pattern; the tested circuit gathers spatial neighborhoods in cellular automata. Models include MLPs, so this is not a test restricted to attention-only transformers.
No training-time onset measurements, loss-curve bump analysis, or timing comparison with an in-context-learning gain.
Does not test large transformers or whether induction heads account for most language-model in-context learning.

Tests trained two-layer transformers in three cellular-automaton settings and two layer-1 designs, but not multiple model families, a size sweep, multiple training runs, other architectures, or modalities.
Does not isolate changes in data or training setup to test their effects on whether or when induction forms or whether in-context learning persists.
Does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or compare induction heads with alternative few-shot mechanisms.
Does not measure the training-time sequence or number of transitions in head formation.

relationships.condition: Trained Shared-head and Dedicated-heads two-layer models on 1D V=2, 1D V=3 and 2D von Neumann cellular automata, read as a spatial generalization of the two-layer composed induction circuit.
relationships.reason: Layer 1 attends to the predicted routing cells and Layer 2 to matching precedents (A01–A12). Masking those positions lowers accuracy while matched random masks barely matter (A13–A36). Magnitudes are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Layer 1 attended to predicted routing cells and layer 2 to matching precedents; masking those positions reduced accuracy while matched random masks had little effect.

source_check.label: supports
